in_arabic.name: مثَر
in_arabic.long_meaning: مثَر هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي، ومعناه مكان عال ومشرف، ويتضمن معاني السمو والرفعة والكرامة، وله دلالات إسلامية ترتبط بالكرامة والاحترام، ويستخدم في التسمية الإسلامية لتحمل معاني السمو الروحي والقيم العالية

in_urdu.name: مثَر
in_urdu.long_meaning: مثَر ایک عربی اصل کا نام ہے، جس کا مطلب بلند و مشرف مقام ہے، اور اس میں عظمت، اعزاز، اور وقار کی معانی شامل ہیں، اور اس کا استعمال اسلامی ناموں میں روحانی بلندی اور उच्च اصولوں کی نمائندگی کرتا ہے

in_hindi.name: मथर
in_hindi.long_meaning: मथर एक अरबी मूल का नाम है, जिसका अर्थ उच्च और सम्मानित स्थान है, और इसमें महानता, सम्मान, और गरिमा के अर्थ शामिल हैं, और इसका उपयोग इस्लामी नामों में आध्यात्मिक उन्नति और उच्च मूल्यों की प्रतिनिधित्व करता है

in_pashto.name: مثر
in_pashto.long_meaning: مثر یو عربي ریښه لرونکی نوم دی، چې د هغه معنا لوړ او مشرف ځای دی، او په هغه کې لوړتیا، عزت، او وقار شامل دي، او د هغه کارونې اسلامي نومونو کې د روحاني لوړتیا او لوړو ارزښتونو ښکارندوی کوي

in_english.name: Mathar
in_english.long_meaning: Mathar is an Arabic origin name, meaning high and honorable place, and includes meanings of greatness, respect, and dignity, and its usage in Islamic names represents spiritual elevation and high values, and is associated with strong personality traits and noble character

pronunciation.urdu: مثَر کی تلفظ میں مہربانی سے اور تھوڑا سا جھومتا ہوا لہجہ
pronunciation.hindi: मथर का उच्चारण में मध्यम स्वर और थोड़ा झूमता हुआ लहजा

data.cultural_impact: The name Mathar holds a significant cultural impact as it is reminiscent of the golden age of Islam when the companions of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) courageously rode horses to spread the message of peace, love, and unity across various nations. It is a reminder of their unwavering dedication, resilience, and fortitude in spreading the religion of Islam. The name reflects the adventurous spirit of the early Muslims and their fearless nature in confronting challenges and adversities.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Mathar embodies the concept of 'Amr Bil Ma'ruf Nahi Anil Munkar' - enjoining good and forbidding evil. This is a fundamental Islamic principle that calls upon every Muslim to strive towards compassion, truth, and righteousness, while shunning evil, transgression, and injustice. The name Mathar further reinforces the importance of community engagement, unity, and solidarity, as it represents the collective efforts of the companions in spreading Islam. It serves as an inspiration for Muslims to continue the legacy of the early believers, by embodying the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) in their daily lives and striving to create a better world for all.

historical_references.context: Mathar was a place in Palestine, mentioned as the site of a major battle during the Muslim conquest of Palestine. The Muslim forces, led by Khalid ibn al-Walid, defeated a Byzantine army under the command of the Marwan ibn Hakim there.

historical_references.context: Mathar is also mentioned as a place in Yemen where a battle between the Zaydi and Umayyad forces took place. The Zaydi forces, led by al-Mansur billah, defeated the Umayyads there.
